newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysian U.M. Land plans high-tech town.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian U.M. Land plans high-tech town.

text.p: Malaysian property company United Malayan Land Bhd (U.M. Land) said on Thursday it was developing an 848-acre (343.2-hectare) piece of land into a 1.2 billion ringgit ($484 million) integrated township.
The township would lie between Malaysia's upcoming administrative capital of Putrajaya and the new Kuala Lumpur International Airport, U.M. Land said in a statement.
The firm is acquiring the land from PERNAS Properties Sdn Bhd for 68.2 million ringgit via a share swap.
The Bangi Heights township will comprise residential, commercial and industrial complexes, and would include a five-star hotel, a shopping mall, a college and a private hospital.
The area would be linked to the Multimedia Super Corridor, a forthcoming high-technology area, by fibre optic links, said Yap Yew Wah, U.M. Land's property development manager.
It would also house an industrial park with research and development facilities for high-technology tenants, Yap told Reuters.
The development cost of 1.2 billion ringgit would be spread over 12 to 14 years, he said.
U.M. Land, which is controlled by Pernas International Holdings Bhd, is also building a 5.5 billion ringgit ($2.2 billion) township in the southern state of Johor.

U.M. Land stock was suspended on Tuesday at 6.00 ringgit pending the land acquisition news. The company's financial controller Lee Kar Fook said he expected the stock to be requoted on Thursday afternoon or on Friday.
